cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus, is writing a letter to the believers in Rome. He's been talking about God's law, and now he gets personal. He starts with something he says we all know: the law is spiritual.

cards.question: Paul says the law is spiritual. Then he says "but" and turns to himself. How does Paul describe himself?

answers.text: Unspiritual and sold as a slave to sin
Spiritual and ready to keep the law
Strong and free from the pull of sin

cards.text: Then Paul says something anybody with a snooze button understands: "I do not understand what I do." You set the alarm to get up early. It goes off. And your OWN thumb hits snooze. Whose thumb IS that?

cards.question: Paul says he does exactly what he wants to do and stays away from what he hates.

cards.text: So Paul keeps doing what he doesn't want to do. Then he stops and works out what that says about God's law.

cards.question: If Paul does what he doesn't want to do, what does he say he's admitting about God's law?

answers.text: That the law is too hard

cards.question: Paul says that in that case, it's no longer really him doing it. It's ___ living in him that does it.

cards.text: Paul gets even more honest. He says he knows nothing good lives in him, that is, in his flesh. No sugarcoating. Not even a sprinkle on top.

cards.question: Paul says he has no desire at all to do what is good.

cards.text: Paul circles back. He doesn't do the good he wants, and he keeps doing the evil he doesn't want. Then that line again: it's sin living in him that does it. Friend, I KNOW this loop. Every night I say, Dorin, NO tasting the dough. Then I look down and the bowl is HALF EMPTY.

cards.question: After going around and around, Paul says he's discovered a principle. What is it?

answers.text: When he wants to do good evil is right there with him
When he wants to do good it gets a little easier
When he obeys the law sin leaves him alone

cards.question: Deep down, in his inner being, Paul says he ___ in God's law.

cards.text: But Paul isn't done. He sees another law in there, and it is picking a FIGHT.

cards.question: Paul sees another law at work in his ___, warring against the law of his ___.
Paul says this other law at work in his body holds him captive to the law of sin that dwells within him.

cards.text: Paul has been honest this whole time, and now it all pours out: "What a wretched man I am!" No joke from me here, friend. I've been stuck in the dark. I know that cry.

cards.question: Paul cries out that he's wretched, held captive by sin. What does he ask?

answers.text: Who will rescue him from this body of death
Why God gave the law in the first place
How much longer he has to keep trying

cards.question: Right after that cry, Paul's tone turns and he gives thanks. Who does Paul thank?

answers.text: God through Jesus Christ our Lord
The apostles who taught him the law
The believers who prayed for him

cards.question: Paul sums it up by saying that with his mind he serves the law of sin, and with his flesh he serves the law of God.
